items.artist: Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy
items.excerpt:
Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release,
Under an Endless Sky
.
In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari,
Songs of Compassion
is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics.
Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: Tako Toki 的第二张专辑延续了首张的多元拼贴路线，乐队成员亲手用废旧物品制作了全部演奏乐器，包括所谓的 tassofon、tubofone、kitchenofon 等。评论特别指出这些自制乐器在现代录音麦克风下依然保持了准确的音高与丰富的音质，展现出乐手精湛的手工与演奏技艺。专辑在风格上跨越广泛，klezmer 小调的欢笑单簧管与巴松对话，cumbia 灵感下的西班牙合唱与拉丁打击乐层次饱满，afrobeat 框架中散落木块与摇铃，samba 节拍里长笛游走，中东旋律则呈现类似六十年代间谍片主题曲的恍惚感。这张作品以垃圾为材，却精准地回应了世界各地节奏、旋律与和声传统的共通之处。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: Camilla Hole Trio 的这张专辑延续了上一张作品中探索挪威传统音乐与现代声响的思路，将斯堪的纳维亚民间旋律置于爵士即兴的框架内展开。Hole 以高音萨克斯为主奏乐器，与贝斯和鼓的对话并非固定分工，三人在演奏中频繁交换旋律与节奏主导权，乐器角色始终处于流动状态。Kalman 的模块化合成器和 Nesheim 的颤音琴作为色彩层叠加，模糊了原声乐器与电子声响之间的界限。开场曲"Springleik"取材自挪威西部传统曲调，原本是用于伴随"Springleik"舞蹈的旋律，乐团在保留这一民间骨架的同时，将其引向自由即兴的延展，使传统素材获得了脱离原本语境的开放性表达。专辑整体呈现出一种介于北欧民谣、前卫爵士与实验声响之间的跨界质地。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这张由瑞典小提琴手Mats Edén、挪威竖笛与萨克斯手Tellef Kvifte及其子、鼓手与作曲家Knut Kvifte Nesheim组成的专辑，以各自国家为主的传统舞曲为素材，却避开适合舞蹈的演出方式，转向三人紧密而私密的室内乐式对话。编曲通过跨风格乐器、即兴片段、突发停滞和模糊的织体，揭示舞曲表面欢乐之下阴暗、神秘的一面。开篇选用挪威Setesdal的水怪传说曲Fossgrimen尤为意味深长，呼应小提琴与瀑布精灵及“魔鬼乐器”的民间阴影。

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items.body: Marvin Tate Controlled Burn Chicago slam poet teams up with Wilco’s LeRoy Bach for an album of avant-soul storytelling and hallucinatory instrumentation Controlled Burn by Marvin Tate Whether you’re just the right amount of tapped-in to Marvin Tate or whether Controlled Burn is your first encounter with the esteemed Chicago poet-performer, you’ll soon realise there’s little else quite like him. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是芝加哥诗人兼表演者Marvin Tate与Wilco成员LeRoy Bach的合作作品。Tate以忧郁的口语朗诵为线索，Bach则提供弹性十足、近乎幻觉化的器乐编排，涵盖吉他、键盘与电子音效等多层次音色。两人在叙事上保持玩味姿态，难以分辨文字与配器孰先孰后。整体而言，Bach的编曲倾向于跟随Tate的呼吸节奏展开，使朗诵文本与即兴化的声响之间形成松散而紧密的对话。这种融合街头诗歌与实验器乐的做法在独立厂牌Amalgam Records的语境下显得自然，作品不追求流行旋律而强调氛围与叙事的模糊张力，适合对跨界实验文本感兴趣的听众。

items.body: Review by meurdhek — We are dealing here with a genuine little zeuhl gem, for which Alain Lebon from Soleil Zeuhl can never be thanked enough for having rescued it from limbo, and which is bound to stir a few emotions.The listener is completely immersed in a zeuhl cauldron, with the sometimes strange yet very pleasant impression of hearing an unreleased tape from Magma's best years. The sound of Carmina, apart from a few forays into soprano saxophone and vibraphone, is very close to that of peak Magma from 1973?74.The group never repeats itself, offering ideas that are each more Magma-esque and zeuhl-driven than the last. This will undoubtedly delight fans of zeuhl music, but it also has the drawback, in my view, of slightly disorienting the listener, who may search in vain for a guiding thread within this very rich and ambitious music.One gets the impression that the band makes it a point of honor never to repeat itself and to constantly surprise the listener. Ideas come thick and fast at a sustained pace, and none is ever truly developed or explored, as the music quickly moves on to something else without any real connection between them.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑被乐评视为一颗真正的zeuhl珍宝，由Soleil Zeuhl厂牌的Alain Lebon从遗忘中抢救出来。其声音气质与Magma 1973-74年巅峰时期极为接近，仅在女高音萨克斯与颤音琴的运用上稍作探索。乐评指出乐队以不断变化、绝不重复为荣，创意密集涌现且节奏持续推进，但每段想法均未被充分展开便迅速转向下一段落，乐曲之间缺乏明确的衔接逻辑。这种做法既展现出zeuhl语汇的丰富性与野心，也可能令听众在如此高密度的信息流中迷失方向，难以找到贯穿全作的引导线索。对于熟悉Magma及其后继者的听众而言，这是一张兼具致敬意味与独立探索价值的作品。

items.body: “Rub’a’Dub Love” is 8-bit digital reggae in the style of the 1980s, and it originally appeared on the album Where My Style Comes From, released in June. On 2 October it came back in two remixes on UK-based digital dub and reggae label Superchip: raggamuffin boom-bap from Hopebullet, a DJ and sound engineer from Osaka who also goes by Ranking Jin, and a second version by RJD. Behind it are deejay Daddy Cookiz and producer Simma, with singer Ponchita Peligros as guest. Simma is Nathan Simm from Hull, England, a producer and DJ who started out in Ableton during the 2020 lockdown, runs Superchip and also records as Polyecho and Square Nath. His 2024 debut, Simma Enters The Game, mixed digital reggae, dubbed-out hip-hop and 8-bit chiptune and drew on the German label Jahtari and the Scottish sound system Mungo’s Hi Fi. Daddy Cookiz has deejayed since 2005 and grew up on Jamaican sound system culture, and he takes his cues from Super Cat, Yellowman and Shabba Ranks. On the album he deejays in that rub-a-dub tradition over Simma’s digital sound, and Simma now takes that sound to Japan, where he performs with Hopebullet in Kyoto on 10 October, Tokyo on 19 October and Yokohama on 21 October, in a showcase for Superchip. Stream “Rub’a’Dub Love (Hopebullet Remix)” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Simma – Rub’a’Dub Love (Hopebullet Remix) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Israeli gothic metal band Fatum Aeternum has rebuilt “P.W.Y.P.” for a streaming release, bringing the track back from their 2012 EP “The Sermon.” The self-released single went out digitally on 25 September 2026. The new version keeps the original ’80s glam-rooted guitar riff while adding aggressive male vocals, a female counter voice, cello and a full gospel choir. Where the 2012 recording leaned on social commentary, the rebuilt arrangement expands it into a more layered, theatrical gothic sound the band describes as a dark sermon. “P.W.Y.P.” is the second single in Fatum Aeternum’s renewed run of releases, following the comeback single “As Above, So Below” on 25 August 2026. That single introduced a new six-piece lineup – Steve Gershin, Evelyn Shor Gershin, Dr. Joe, Victor Grassiano, Max Datskovsky and Mark Muzykant – which also plays on “P.W.Y.P.” The track was recorded at Lodge Studios in Northampton, UK. Denis Saenko handled mixing and mastering, with additional mixing by Gershin; Tayo Olawepo arranged and recorded the choir. The band’s promotional materials cite Lacrimosa, Therion and Haggard as reference points. “P.W.Y.P.” is available to stream on Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Amazon Music, Deezer and SoundCloud. About Fatum Aeternum Fatum Aeternum formed in Tel Aviv, Israel, in 2006, built around Steve Gershin on mandolin, bass and vocals, alongside Ze’ev Gut on fiddle and vocals and Olga Braverman on flute and vocals. The group’s first full lineup added Ilya Surnin on drums, Dan Yoffe on guitar and Rivka Aizenberg on viola, playing a self-described “renaissance metal” blend of folk and metal. Braverman left in 2007 and Gut in 2008, staying on as a guest musician as the band shifted toward a heavier, more electrified sound. Gershin considered disbanding the group in 2009 and recorded a memorial album of earlier material instead; Evelyn Shor Gershin joined permanently around the same time, stabilising the lineup. The band re-recorded its debut album “This Dream Is Dead” several times before releasing it on CD in 2011. On 24 September 2011, Fatum Aeternum played the 12th Children of the Night Gothic Festival in Kyiv, Ukraine, its first show outside Israel, sharing the bill with Waves Under Water and Diary of Dreams. The video for “Apocalypse Now” followed on YouTube in April 2012 and aired on MTV Israel’s “Headbangers Ball” that June. The band self-released the EP “The Sermon” in September 2012, recorded at Lodge Studios in Northampton, UK, and opened for Apoptygma Berzerk the same month before going on hiatus in 2013. Gershin and Evelyn Shor Gershin rebuilt the lineup with George Falk and Igor May in 2014, releasing the single “One Bastard” that April and the maxi-single “The Pain” later the same year. The EP “The Darkest Hour” followed in 2015, then “Mass Suicide of Human Race” in 2017 and “Singing Songs of Desperation” in 2020. Fatum Aeternum returned in 2026 after a three-year gap, a pause the band’s own site attributes to health issues within the group. The comeback single “As Above, So Below” arrived on 25 August 2026 with a new six-piece lineup of Gershin, Evelyn Shor Gershin, Dr. Joe, Victor Grassiano, Max Datskovsky and Mark Muzykant. “P.W.Y.P.,” a rebuilt version of the 2012 “The Sermon” track, follows as the second single in that renewed run.
items._cn_summary: 以色列哥特金属乐队Fatum Aeternum将2012年EP《The Sermon》中的“P.W.Y.P.”重新编排，作为2026年9月25日发行的流媒体单曲。新版保留八十年代华丽摇滚风格的吉他 riff，加入更具攻击性的男声、女声对唱、大提琴及完整福音合唱团，使原本带有社会评论意味的作品扩展为层次更丰富的戏剧化“黑暗布道”式演绎。歌曲是新六人阵容继《As Above, So Below》后的第二支作品，在英国Lodge Studios录制，制作与混音由Denis Saenko等参与，合唱团由Tayo Olawepo编曲录制，并以Lacrimosa、Therion、Haggard为参考方向。文章以新闻报道与乐队背景介绍为主，缺少对录音质量的深入评价。

items.body: There is a particular kind of youthful ambition that treats a synthesizer’s limitations as somebody else’s problem. If the arrangement feels crowded, another drum track might settle the argument; if the equipment begins to struggle, perhaps it needs to be programmed harder. Baltimore’s Pygmy Children remember their earliest recordings with the affectionate candor of two people who have since learned exactly what they were putting their machines through. More than thirty years later, those experiments are getting a fresh listen. Out now through Re:Mission Entertainment, Malignant: Redux revisits the electro-industrial duo’s 1994 debut album, Malignant, and the preceding 1993 EP, Facedown. Released October 2, the collection brings brothers Pete and Brian Roper back to the recordings that introduced them to the American industrial underground, with the digital edition collecting both releases in full. Originally recorded at Hit and Run Studios in Rockville, Maryland, with engineer Steve Carr, the material has received its first official remaster from Jeff Mortimer at JM Mastering. Brian Roper supplies the Redux artwork, completing a return to a period when the duo’s appetite for dense arrangements regularly outpaced the resources at their disposal. The brothers describe those sessions with refreshing frankness: “Admittedly, the record sounds pretty raw. We were novices trying to create something multi-layered and frenetic, working with what we had and probably not fully knowing what the hell we were doing, just going for it. Some of the synths were being pushed to the point of voice exhaustion, while multiple drum tracks pounded away simultaneously. Looking back, some editing was probably in order, but the intention was always there. We may not have hit the target exactly, but the aim was definitely there.” That willingness to admit the excess is part of the appeal. Their account describes two musicians learning through accumulation, pursuing an idea until the equipment itself began to object. The early titles suggest a similarly restless approach: Core moves between Resistance and Meltdown, while Facedown appears in Reflex, Manic, Bootstamp, and Dead versions across the digital collection. Even the track listing seems reluctant to leave an experiment alone. For Re:Mission founder Wes Turner, the release also carries a personal connection. Pygmy Children helped shape his taste in dark electronic music during the 1990s; three decades on, his label is releasing both their new work and these formative recordings. Turner now gets to put the records that helped educate him back into other listeners’ hands. Listen to Malignant : Redux below: Malignant : Redux by Pygmy Children Pygmy Children first surfaced with Facedown on Noname/Noslogan Productions, following it with Malignant before moving on to Deconstruct, released by Cleopatra in 1995, and Low Life Dream, issued through Sub/Mission Records and Out Of Line in 1998. After years away, the brothers returned in 2025 through Re:Mission with Coincidental Strategies, accompanied by singles including I Have No Name and Signal Unknown. Their recent single Proof in Lies, which we covered in August, leads their forthcoming fifth studio album, Into The Silence. With new material underway, Malignant : Redux offers a timely return to the duo’s beginnings. The brothers can now afford to smile at their early excesses, though the synthesizers they used back then may still be entitled to an apology. Malignant : Redux is available digitally and on CD via Re:Mission Entertainment. Order here or find additional listening options here. Digital edition: Both Malignant and Facedown in full, comprising 16 tracks. Limited digipak CD: An edition of 100 copies, containing Malignant plus Fear, the B-side from the Facedown EP, with the digital edition included. Three-CD autographed bundle: Malignant : Redux alongside autographed original pressings of Malignant and Facedown, plus the digital edition. Limited to 25 bundles, with US shipping only. items.body: With Economy of Movement, Antipodean breakbeat pioneer Social Sport delivers five restless, shape-shifting cuts where fractured rhythms, heavyweight bass and psychedelic atmospheres turn the breakbeat tradition into something fiercely alive and forward-moving. Five cuts of seriously diverse breakbeat chicanery Economy of Movement by Social Sport   Antipodean breakbeat pioneer Social Sport knows what time it is. Economy of Movement arrives as five cuts of seriously diverse breakbeat chicanery, ranging across the territory occupied by beats that have escaped the tyranny of the 1 and 3. Because that, essentially, is the point: breakbeat breaks the line. Kicks bounce and lurch, snares and claps shuffle, hi-hats stammer and skitter, creating pace, tension and the possibility of movement in the spaces between expectation. Mr Sport understands these theatrics and deploys them with integrity and valor, honoring the traditions and foundations through which creator, creativity and the creative œuvre continually collide. “Inflow” opens with serious intent. Kicks move through silver atmospheres of mountain mist and textural haze, summoning elemental forces and earthly gravitas. “Life” then takes the Amen break on a tangential excursion, all aplomb and swagger, building rolling thunder from didgeridoos and chopped vocal commands. There’s something here that, to my ears at least, accidentally invokes the gods of FSOL’s “Papua New Guinea.” Not pastiche. Not homage. Something more interesting: an apparently necessary Occidental parallel evolution. Grit and grift rendered kinetic :: “Movement Economy” introduces stop-start rhythms and female vocal fragments into a 2-step-adjacent landscape of spring-loaded didges and ticking-time-bomb mood swings. Dark? Perhaps. But I don’t really read darkness here as darkness. I read power. Necessity. Seriousness. Grit and grift rendered kinetic. Tight and sick as one. “Still Working On It” brings the archetypal breakbeat throwdown: reverbed 303, filtering synth tapestries and enough dancefloor adjacency to make the whole thing twitch. It’s a proper closer, exiting with a kablamo and the brand-new stallion hoofs of badassery. Then LOIF gets involved, reworking the title track by diving beneath its surface and finding more room in the apparent darkness. The bottom end comes forward, the drums sharpen, and the bass assumes a more pronounced riff-like presence. Above it, silver clouds of smog and illumination hover while acid swirls stripe the walls with psychedelic color. It’s a redub, a reroute and a conversation with the original. More importantly, it completes the circle: five tracks that collectively reveal the specificity of an artist’s particular lens, and the possibilities that emerge when movement is allowed to escape its economy. From the other side of the globe, I see you.​ Kudos. The work is superb. Economy of Movement is available on Steeplejack. items.body: Mathias Villard is a very promising sound artist and Past Radiance can easily figure among my top favorite albums for this year. Exquisite, wistful, cinematic, alluring and emotionally transportive. For fans of Alessandro Cortini, Bvdub, Loscil, Markus Fjellström and Terence Hannum. Once more, Affin proves to be in the first league concerning modern-day ambient-lush drone music. The album flows like a gigantic oceanic movement Past Radiance by Mathias Villard   Mathias Villard is a French sound artist now based in Düsseldorf, Germany. He is a new face in the world of ambient-drone and orchestral cinematic electronica, but his debut album finds the best possible way to bring it to a larger international audience, thanks to a contract with key indie label Affin (headed by Joachim Spieth). Affin already presents an immense catalog of advanced electronic music with a strong interest in densely layered soundscapes, emotional cinematic escapism and ambient-techno waves. Numerous well-established projects and names are part of the catalogue, among others Pepo Galán and Markus Guentner (with his magnificent Black Dahlia reviewed on Igloo). Past Radiance appears to be a high-class textured ambient release with a strong melodious-moody component that will leave you speechless. If you are fond of lush sonic textures and enveloping electronic sequences sustained by grainy repetitive melodies surrounded by a vast, spacious aura, there is no doubt that this album will reach your heart. The gently sinuous parts and soothing ambiences are powerfully seconded by deep and slowly bassy lines which definitely add more depth and strength to the pieces. Difficult to pick out one piece in particular, as the album flows like a gigantic oceanic movement with rare sonic engulfment. Some lighter moments appear from time to time :: In a track such as “Debris,” this mysterious sonic approach and spacious treatment reach full development: a really massive, cascading and compelling piece. This album integrates a sumptuous sense of motion which meets quite devastating, heart-stirring, almost gloomy but always pleasant melodies. Some lighter moments appear from time to time, as in the curiously pulsating, chilling and bassy “Haze.” The success of this album lies in the meticulously crafted compositional mode but also in the solid technical production. All in all, Mathias Villard is a very promising sound artist and his album can easily figure among my top favorite albums for this year. Exquisite, wistful, cinematic, alluring and emotionally transportive. For fans of Alessandro Cortini, Bvdub, Loscil, Markus Fjellström and Terence Hannum. Once more, this label proves to be in the first league concerning modern-day ambient-lush drone music. Past Radiance is available on Affin. items.body: EYAA takes its name from a cry of encouragement tied to trance. The French-Ghanaian trio put out “Luku Luku” on Sharma Records on 2 October, the first of five singles leading to their first EP. The voice is Kyekyeku‘s, a singer and guitarist from Accra who now lives in Bayonne, in south-west France, and has worked with highlife veterans Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor. He formed the seven-piece Ah! Kwantou in 2019, and two of its members, bassist Kevin Bucquet and drummer Fred Faure, are the other two thirds of EYAA. In EYAA, Bucquet plays synths and runs the machines as well as the bass, and he, Faure and Kyekyeku composed “Luku Luku” together, with Kyekyeku writing the words. Kyekyeku sings in Twi, pidgin and English over Faure’s drums and Bucquet’s bass, with synths and machines adding the electronics, and the grooves draw on afro-funk, highlife and afrobeat to make an afro-electro built for dancing. This year the trio has played in France, in Accra at Les Francophonies Festival, and in Portugal at Tom de Festa Festival in Tondela. items.body: The Australian band Chiron is back with their latest album, a project three years in the making. Led by frontman Michael Aliani (ex-IKON) and joined by bassist Dino Molinaro (IKON) and guitarist Ivan Bullock, the band presents nine tracks plus four additional remixes. Those familiar with Chiron will hardly be surprised by the influences and style: the music is a fusion of Dark-Wave and Post-Punk. The dark atmosphere that permeates the album occasionally evokes memories of Joy Division, with a pervasive sense of darkness and melancholy running throughout. The guitar sometimes takes on a psychedelic edge, adding an interesting touch, while the synth elements provide an additional melodic dimension. Yvette Winkler (Vaselyne) was invited to collaborate on the final track. The additional remixes are far from ordinary; one of them, for instance, features vocals from the cold and charismatic Kriistal Ann (Paradox Obscur). They lean slightly more towards Electro, at times incorporating a more club-oriented vibe. Chiron has never disappointed me, and with “A Dark Beauty”, the band has once again delivered a top-notch album. Personally, however, I have a particular soft spot for the slightly heavier tracks. (Rating:8). Listen to “A Dark Beauty”: A Dark Beauty by Chiron About Chiron Chiron formed in Melbourne, Australia, in 1997, founded by vocalist Michael Aliani after he left the Australian darkwave band Ikon. The project debuted with “Eve” in 1999 on the Italian label Energeia, followed by “Slipping Away” (2005, Apollyon Records), the “Breaking Point” EP (2009) and the album “We Own the Night” (2015). A compilation, “Chiron: The Best Of”, appeared on Brazil’s Wave Records the same year. The band’s 2022 album “The Sun Goes Down” marked its move to Dark Vinyl Records and brought founding Ikon bassist Dino Molinaro back into the lineup. For “A Dark Beauty”, released 17 July 2026 through Dark Vinyl Records, the band worked as a trio of Aliani on vocals and electronics, Molinaro on bass and Ivan Bullock on guitar and electronics, with Ernie Oppenheimer producing, mixing and mastering. Guest contributions come from Vaselyne‘s Yvette Winkler and Paradox Obscur‘s Kriistal Ann on the album’s remix section, extending the darker, guitar-forward direction the band set on its previous release.

items.body: Being yourself has become a surprisingly laborious business. The photograph needs editing, the opinion needs prompting, and loneliness must be presented to resemble an enviable evening. A social media profile offers the freedom to create the person we wish we were, then puts that person to work around the clock. Before long, algorithmic approval starts behaving like a drug, desire becomes a recurring payment, and the supposedly liberated individual is checking in with the platform every few minutes. The mask has developed an excellent social life, but its owner could probably use some company. Berlin’s XTR HUMAN, the long-running project of musician Johannes Stabel, turns that predicament into a forceful EBM workout on “Fake,” shared ahead of its October 9 release through Wie Ein Gott Records. The first release in a new series, the single was recorded at Infinite Power Studios in Los Angeles, with Matia Simovich handling production and mixing. Its entirely analog construction puts the emphasis on force, repetition, and the persuasive pull of an electronic beat. “Fake” opens with a metallic bass synth line that gives its EBM groove a distinctly funky gait. There is plenty of force in the repetition, though the low end knows how to move its hips. Stabel’s vocals land with a slap, a club-driven Neue Deutsche Welle drawl carrying the rhythmic confidence and insolent phrasing of hip-hop. He makes each phrase feel physically involved in the beat, pushing the groove forward with a delivery that sounds thoroughly pleased with its own bad intentions. The synth melody brings to mind the peculiar electronic funk of Fad Gadget’s “Lady Shave,” while the track’s muscular structure shares more with the disciplined body music of fellow Mute artists DAF and Nitzer Ebb. Simovich’s production keeps those elements sharply defined: the bass has weight, the rhythm has room to work, and the melody provides enough mischief to make the machinery feel dangerously inviting. That invitation is central to the song’s themes. “Fake” confronts digital isolation, manufactured identities, and the ease with which desire becomes dependency. Profiles turn into disguises; the pursuit of recognition keeps the person behind them performing. The track’s repeated patterns give that cycle a bodily form, suggesting the exhausting business of moving constantly while getting nowhere. Stabel makes the predicament sound seductive, which is precisely how such arrangements secure our cooperation in the first place. Listen to “Fake” below: “Fake” is out October 9, 2026 via Wie Ein Gott Records. Find the single here on release day. Alongside Simovich’s production and mixing, the recording credits include assistant engineers Coleman Ketchem and Grover Greenberg, with mastering by Bonati Mastering. Johannes Stabel began XTR HUMAN in 2012, developing a project whose early coldwave and post-punk interests have expanded into industrial electronics, techno, and EBM. His rich vocal delivery gives those harder rhythms a recognizable personality, drawing together German-language phrasing, new wave melody, and the propulsion of body music. Albums such as G.O.L.D in 2021 and Schrank in 2024 established a catalogue equally interested in dancefloor movement and social criticism. Earlier this year, the Rave God EP brought ’90s rave energy into that combination, including a remix by Houses of Heaven. Stabel’s international live history includes Wave-Gotik-Treffen and Absolution Festival, alongside appearances with artists including Die Selektion, Qual, Lebanon Hanover, and She Past Away. This month’s shows include a return to Los Angeles for Substance at The Belasco, followed by Berlin’s Unterwelt Festival on Halloween. Upcoming 2026 live dates: October 8 — Denton, TX — Rubber Gloves Rehearsal Studios October 9 — Austin, TX — Cheer Up Charlies (NITE SCHOOL) October 15 — Spokane, WA — Red Room Lounge October 16 — Portland, OR — The Coffin (Halloween Fetish Ball) October 17 — Seattle, WA — The Mountain Room October 24 — Los Angeles, CA — The Belasco (Substance) October 31 — Berlin, Germany — Festsaal Kreuzberg (Unterwelt Festival) Follow XTR HUMAN: Website Facebook Instagram YouTube Bandcamp Spotify Cover photograph by Anni Porrasmäki. items.body: Dau, the moniker of UK ambient musician Phil Self, is about to release his solo debut, Zed Zed. Arriving via Phantom Limb’s new sub-label imprint Spirituals, which promotes ‘high grade, emotive ambient and experimental music from emerging artists from across the world’, Zed Zed is a beautifully-crafted and intricately-woven record, utilising classical chamber orchestration and blending it with an ambient core. Self is involved in many other projects, from the UK instrumental sextet yndi halda to performing in the live band of folk-rock singer-songwriter Will Varley. Self also runs the Isolation Choir, a non-profit initiative for the elderly and the vulnerable, where musicians and non-musicians alike are invited to contribute remotely to pieced-together ensemble performances (the first video of which caught the eye of Brian Eno, who was so moved by the performance and the compassionate message behind the project that he offered his services for the second). Zed Zed features bowed guitar, reed organ, and voice, but Self also includes recordings of water bowls, falling rain, and sounds from his kitchen, which produces a warm, comfortable, and homely atmosphere, adding degrees of personality and intimacy within the familiar environment of home. The human qualities of empathy, kindness, and care are literally at the centre of the music, a point at which it can brightly shine, and it also reflects Self’s own personality, the music acting as a conduit for his inner kindness. The music unravels with patience, slowly developing and building upon itself. Perhaps most importantly, Zed Zed is free of computer processing; digital editing and computer interference is rejected. The record is entirely acoustic and proud of the fact, featuring real-time performances and nothing but acoustic instrumentation. A deep ambient heart beats within its music, which is all the more evident in the dulled harmonic resonance of its water bowl. And along with the sound of dripping water, reverberating gongs help to produce calming sensations and feelings of immense relief. With graceful movements, the music never seems to put a foot wrong. ‘Sundowning’ closes the album as an overlapping family of lean, slanting strings provide the last flares of light. Even with the sunset and its representation of ending and finality, the music’s message is one of enduring beauty, optimism, and appreciation, retaining its grace right up until its end. items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以中提琴、管风琴、击弦古钢琴和钢琴为核心乐器，辅以鼓、贝斯与合成器，呈现出模糊而流动的质感。乐评指出作品大量采用即兴演奏，常以单次录音完成，贯穿持续的低音嗡鸣，营造出近乎神秘、静谧的氛围。音乐融合民谣、前卫实验与宗教感的冥想特质，歌词取材于英国自然诗人约翰·克莱尔的诗作，旋律具有跨越时代的古老感。中心曲目《Sprigs of Heather》从中世纪圣咏般的开场发展为钢琴主导的缓慢级进旋律，被形容为完美的小品。专辑亦是Cotton对2024年末去世父亲的纪念之作，弥漫着失落与柔情，光与暗在乐句间交替渗透，整体音乐拒绝被简单归类，以其私密而独特的美学自成一体。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦贝宁乐手Antoine Dougbé与Orchestre Poly-Ritmo在1977至1982年间的合作录音。Dougbé以双手拍击大腿演绎Cavacha节奏著称，该律动由鼓手Belobi Meridjo从火车节奏中提炼，后广泛渗透至1970年代中期的刚果流行音乐中。Dougbé本人是伏都教（vodun）实践者，被称为"魔鬼首相"，只与Poly-Ritmo合作，认为其他乐队无法实现他的音乐构想。合辑收录其三张专辑及部分单曲，展现了萨托与萨帕塔节奏与古巴son影响的交织，合成器与闪烁吉他音色已带有八十年代的塑料质感，但根基仍扎在七十年代的放克传统中。《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》以合成器铺底，吉他与高帽主导的律动形成层次；《We Tayi Sin Assi Tche》则更直接地呼应古巴音乐元素，引入持续牛铃与典型的人声对唱结构。Analog Africa厂牌以此为其第44号发行，将这段短暂却极具浓度的录音生涯系统地推向国际听众视野。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — From the title which translates loosely to "loose woman" to the cover of a quasi-mythical physically well appointed female to the generally erotic lyrical themes of the trad and original numbers presented here, TARUJEN SAARI's second album is probably the merriest of their discography. The ensemble continues to present renditions of well known songs from the British Isles as well as their homeland, and once again in each case they offer a novel interpretation.Closest comparisons would be with the more politically serious MABSANT from Wales and GALAHAD from Germany, with the usual British Isles (including JETHRO TULL at their folkiest) and Breton (BERNARD BENOIT) suspects of course, and, in one track ("Lampolan Vintilla"), the as yet unformed SANGRE DE MUERDAGO. "Y� viel� on" has a go at the very first track on the very first CLANNAD album in a manner which, superior or not, fits better on this album than on that Donegal group's debut. It's a good deal more rocking with menacing fiddles. The last 2 songs respectively revisit "Tam Lin" (best known as a FAIRPORT song) and "The Twelve Witches" (STEELEYE SPAN) and to me are unrecognizable from the versions I know, with only the first somewhat signaled by its many verses. It's much more mysterious with whistles and whispered lyrics for the first part but, without following along the Finnish lyrics, I find it stays on past closing time, while I have no issues with "Twelve Witches" at all, a typically dire lyric made joyous, even in Finnish!For the rest, it's all at least good, with the best being "Hepsankaika" which introduces our character "type", the saucy fiddle-heavy "Neidon Kielto", the cello infused and at least R rated "Minulta Saisit", and the seize the day whistled exuberance of "Lampolan Vintill�".Our protagonist can succeed in seducing even the most hardened of us from track one, and isn't that her goal? She does get a lot of help from a band that is a lot more disciplined than she.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是芬兰乐队TARUJEN SAARI的第二张作品，以轻佻女性形象为概念贯穿。从封面到歌词都带有情欲色彩，专辑氛围据称是他们作品中最欢快的。乐队以新颖方式重新演绎英国群岛与芬兰本土的知名民谣曲目，与威尔士的MABSANT和德国的GALAHAD在政治严肃性上有相似气质。专辑对小提琴、口哨、低语人声等元素进行了独特的编配处理，将传统民谣素材转化为更具神秘感和实验性的版本。最后两首分别重新诠释了Fairport的《Tam Lin》和Steeleye Span的《The Twelve Witches》，在保留原曲骨架的同时赋予了全新的芬兰语演绎。

items.body: Silence has a talent for passing itself off as peace. Two people can share a room, exchange the necessary pleasantries, and conduct an entire argument without troubling the air between them. Inside, every withheld accusation is already gathering speed. Given enough time, even “How was your day?” can begin to sound like a contact sport. Milan quartet October take that condition onto the ice in their video for Universe. The fourth single from their debut album, Dancing Like an Idiot, out now through Waddafuzz! Records, follows the uncomfortable distance between what a relationship looks like from the outside and what its participants are putting themselves through within it. A frozen surface can conceal considerable commotion, and October have enlisted a hockey team to give those private collisions a public airing. The song itself has a supple, sophisticated swing. A rhythmic bassline brings the new wave funk of Roxy Music and Japan to mind, its firm articulation keeping the groove grounded as sustained guitar tones stretch above it. The snare lands at deliberate intervals, leaving generous space around each strike. There is a progressive streak in the arrangement, a willingness to let the instrumental passages stretch and change shape without losing the underlying rhythm. Gianluca Villa sings in a silky upper register reminiscent of Peter Gabriel, his measured delivery building to increasingly impassioned peaks on the line “A Message from the stars.” A gentle guitar jangle carries the song forward, lifting some of its emotional weight. A string interlude zigzags through the arrangement as the vocal rises into a high croon, and tension builds until the full force of the performance comes crashing back. Directed and edited by Fabrizio Grasso, with concept and production by Davide Debenedetti for Filmico, the video makes that division visible. October perform on the rink beneath bright backlights, framed against rows of empty seats, while members of Sgularat Hockey Club Milano skate around them in yellow and black. The musicians hold their positions as the players accelerate, compete, and cut across the space between them. Pads, helmets, and sticks give anger and frustration a physical vocabulary; the ice supplies the emotional temperature. There is something both funny and painfully apt about bringing protective equipment into a love song. Here, the action surrounding the band becomes the argument nobody is having aloud: misunderstandings, thwarted attempts at connection, and the helplessness of trying to reach someone who has become difficult to recognise. Grasso lets the rink carry the metaphor, its broad white expanse accommodating all that activity without offering much warmth. Watch the video for Universe below: October formed in Milan in 2024, bringing together musicians whose backgrounds include Grandi Animali Marini, Il Fieno, NOA, and Egokid, alongside collaborations with Veracrash and I Ministri. Villa handles guitar and vocals, joined by bassist Dario Giordano, drummer Paolo Soffientini, and synth player Davide “dEbE” Debenedetti. Their debut was recorded at Casamedusa with Francesco Campanozzi and Frigo Studio with Francesco Ferrari, then mixed and mastered by Paolo Mauri. Released on March 30, 2026, Dancing Like an Idiot is available digitally and on vinyl. Listen to Universe below and order the album here. items._cn_summary: 米兰四人乐队October发布首张专辑中的第四支单曲《Universe》，音乐呈现出柔软而复杂的律动，律动贝斯线让人联想到Roxy Music与Japan的新浪潮放克风味，稳定的颗粒感支撑着上方延展的吉他持续音色。军鼓以刻意间隔落下，器乐段落允许自由拉伸变形而不失底层律脉。Gianluca Villa以丝绸般的高音域演唱，递进式地在高潮处爆发。弦乐间奏穿插于人声高亢的吟唱之间，张力层层堆叠直至全力释放。MV由冰球场作为视觉隐喻，乐队成员在明亮的背光下静止演奏，而冰球运动员在其周围穿梭冲撞，将关系中未言明的误解与隔阂外化为可感知的肢体语言，防护装备与冰面共同构成情感温度的视觉注解。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — This group of Finnish Vikings offers a fascinating blend of styles; they look and sound the part during live performances and draw upon Renaissance elements, not only in their compositions but also in the instruments they play. At the same time, they navigate the realm of hard rock with ease, channeling a raw savagery and boundless, spirited energy that permeates their music, extending all the way to the cover art of Susien Y�-Delirium Lupus.Kaisa Saari sings in her native tongue; alongside the distorted guitar, the sounds of a baroque viola and a traditional Viking lyre emerge in "Nostakaamme Malja," while "Muistanko V��rin" showcases Saari's soprano vocal talents. The violin, mandolin, sitar, and accordion infuse sweetness and depth into the raw power of the electric guitar and drums, creating a perfect symbiosis. It concludes like a song from a mystical forest set in the modern age, where classical elements filter through the branches of towering pines to reach a darkness that light would otherwise never penetrate.Kuninkaan Pidot leans more heavily on classical influences; amidst an acoustic soundscape of guitar and violin, it evokes the late-70s folk era of Jethro Tull, until Tarujen Saari shifts toward psychedelia, as if alcohol were flooding that ancient feast for the senses. The lyrics are an adaptation of a very old traditional British ballad known in English as "King Henry." The song highlights that appearances can be deceiving and that generosity, kindness, and genuine courtesy in the face of the unknown are rewarded with great blessings."Musta Sunnuntai" is a beautiful, powerful instrumental that also brings to mind Amon D��l II. There are also moments of relaxed introspection that evoke Scandinavian winters, possessing a cinematic quality ranging from Nordic noir to Bergman films. Armed with violin and accordion, they create a warm atmosphere that melts the snow; what might initially seem cold or aggressive turns tender, like a hearth glowing in the night.The violin arrangements are progressively symphonic in Palatynen laulu, not to mention the accelerated hard rock that also embodies Celtic tradition with electric guitar riffs in Kunungatar Kristiina.Rumpua ly�k�� kuninkaalle proposes a different atmosphere, reminiscent of those slow blues of Janis Joplin and Big Brother & The Holding Company, making it mystical with some jazzy, yet magical, percussion, making Summertime something dense and completely different. Guest musician Jaakko Rajakisto plays the bagpipes on "Hovitanssi." As "Hemminki Ja Tunturin Noita" plays, one cannot help but notice the unstoppable convergence of progressive power and ethnic harmony, embodied by that violin, recalling certain moments from Curved Air; Kaisa Saari channels the energy of Sonja Kristina across the musical spectrum, while the spirit of Daryl Way is present in Marja Tuhkanen.The surprises keep coming, notably the powerful chorus of "Susien Y�", which carries a most welcome Renaissance-style darkness. The ceremony could only culminate in a moment of delicate, subtle, and epic ecstasy, immortalized in the song "W�in�n viikate."

items._cn_summary: 芬兰乐队Tarujen Saari以北欧异教徒与维京文化为美学根基，将文艺复兴时期乐器（巴洛克中提琴、维京诗琴）与失真电吉他、曼陀林、西塔琴、手风琴并置，形成古典民谣与硬摇滚的奇异共生。主唱Kaisa Saari以芬兰语演唱，展现女高音穿透力，同时融入凯尔特传统电吉他riff与迷幻色彩。专辑在民谣叙事中穿插电影化的北欧冬日意象，器乐编排从Jethro Tull式的原声渐进至交响化小提琴爆发，并在慢拍蓝调段落中加入爵士化打击乐与风笛。歌词改编自英国古老民谣，探讨表象与真诚的辩证。整体呈现出一种扎根于欧洲中世纪与北欧萨米传统的跨时空民俗拼贴。

items.body: Review by UMUR — "For the Love of Art and the Making" is the third full-length studio album by Danish power/progressive metal act Beyond Twilight (if you discount the two Twilight albums as the works ofanother band). The album was released through Massacre Records in April 2006. It�s the successor to"Section X" from March 2005. There has been one lineup change since "Section X" as lead vocalistKelly Sundown Carpenter has been replaced by Swedish singer Bj�rn Jansson."For the Love of Art and the Making" is quite an interesting release as it�s basically one, 37:49minutes long composition broken down into 43 sub tracks. Stylistically it�s a continuation of thepower/progressive metal style of the preceding releases and as Jansson is a suitable and not toodifferent sounding replacement for Carpenter, the change on the lead vocalist spot doesn�t changemuch in terms of consistency of the band�s sound. The many short sub tracks makes "For the Love ofArt and the Making" a very different listening experience though as the tracks form only short partsof a longer track, they don�t have much time to evolve.It�s not that this is simple or one-dimensional music, because the tracks often shift in dynamicsbetween a heavy power/progressive metal oriented approach and more subtle and mellow parts. A normalverse/chorus structured composition wouldn�t work that way because it�s longer and you have time todevelop ideas over the course of a longer playing time. Here the short track lengths mean that ideasare executed fast and they flow by even faster. I�m not sure I think it always work that well,because sometimes I feel Beyond Twilight could have done a lot more with some of the parts, but atthat point they have usually already moved on to the next section. So, although "For the Love of Art and the Making" is a both well produced and well performedrelease, the songwriting approach will probably divide the waters. There�s arguably a lot of qualityhere but as an album I�m not sure I think "For the Love of Art and the Making" works that well. Tomy ears it�s more a study in interesting ideas and high level musicianship. Thinking of "For theLove of Art and the Making" as a single coherent composition doesn�t cross my mind while listeningto the album. The song is constantly disrupted and changes gears and dynamics and it�s actually abit stressful to listen to. When that is said "For the Love of Art and the Making" is still a highquality release, but I�m pretty sure it�s an acquired taste, so enter at your own risk. A 3.5 star(70%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以乌克兰传统民歌为基础，由乌克兰裔加拿大歌手Marichka联合两组音乐人——一组在乌克兰、一组在加拿大——共同录制。器乐以弓弦乐器为主，搭配班杜拉琴、钢琴及罕见的双陶笛，纯粹的弦乐与人声构成质朴而强烈的底色。主题围绕约两万名乌克兰儿童被俄罗斯强行带离家园的战争罪行展开，传统歌词与当代语境交织——《异乡》改编自描述少女被迫外出做工的旧曲，词句双关映射当下被拐儿童的命运；《Rusalka》则以传说中田野与河流的自然精灵为意象，旋律与演唱转向尖锐与激烈。所有成员均为女性，加拿大团队持续巡演以传播这些歌曲。专辑介于传统民谣记录与社会行动之间，以歌声作为见证与抵抗的工具。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�
